name: Archive
tip: XPRS packets — the messages and posts this device writes down. Yours are always kept. Beyond that you decide: the callsigns you follow, and whether strangers get a place too.

children.name: keep_followed
children.label: Keep what people I follow say
children.tip: Their messages and posts are kept for as long as you follow them — no limit and no expiry, the same as your own.

children.name: public
children.label: Public archiver
children.tip: Keep strangers' packets too, within the limit below, and tell the network so (serve:archive). Off, this device keeps nothing for anybody else and announces nothing.

children.name: always_on
children.label: Always on
children.tip: The further promise a plugged-in machine can make: raised budgets, gossip for every callsign, and a place others deposit mail. Needs Public archiver.

name: Files
tip: Files this device hosts for other people, so they survive when the device that made them is offline. Nothing of yours is deleted to make room.

children.name: followed
children.label: Keep files from people I follow

children.name: free_space
children.label: Free space
children.confirm-text: Everything this device is keeping for other people will be deleted. Your own files, and anything you chose to keep, are not touched.

name: Directory
tip: Tells the network which devices hold the posts and files of each npub. It stores addresses, never the content — a directory that goes offline costs the network a phone book, not a library.

name: My archivers
tip: The devices you trust to keep copies of your messages and answer "where can I find you". This station sends them a copy and announces them once a day (t:mailbox). Type a callsign to add one; tap the bin to remove.

children.name: auto
children.label: Auto-select an archiver
children.tip: When on and you have chosen none, a volunteer node keeps your messages. Add a callsign to choose your own instead.

children.name: myarch
children.empty: No archiver chosen. With Auto-select on, a volunteer node keeps your messages; search a callsign to choose your own.
